title: design changes go into their numbered home section, never onto the end of design.md, so parallel tasks stop colliding
acceptance: Why. On 2026-10-03/04, design/design.md conflicted between almost every pair of parallel PRs, and each conflict cost a rebuild round plus a fresh review: resolving it changes the patch-id, and a changed patch-id voids the APPROVE (skills/firstmate/SKILL.md:299-312). An independent review (2026-10-04) found the cause: the conflicting commits were almost pure appends of a new unnumbered `###` section at the very end of the file (T-185 +37/-0, T-125 +36/-0, T-182 +24/-0, T-184 +18/-0, T-180 +17/-0). Nine such sections now follow `### 15.10 Concurrent projects` (design/design.md:4956), at lines 4974 (T-157), 4993 (T-139), 5040 (T-052), 5067 (T-143), 5108 (T-175), 5133 (T-180), 5150 (T-182), 5174 (T-125) and 5210 (T-185), and the file ends at 5245. Every append lands in the same final hunk. The captain approved this plan ('好 照修正版寫spec', 2026-10-04). Rewriting or splitting the file was rejected, because section anchors and normative text must stay.

Relocate.
- Move each of the nine tail sections into the section it belongs to. The home may be a `## N.` section or a numbered `### N.M` subsection.
- If the home has numbered children (for example `### 5.3` with `### 5.3.1`-`5.3.4`, design/design.md:498 and :684-962), the moved section goes at the end of the last numbered child, one heading level deeper than that child, so it stays inside that child's range in `anchors()`. Otherwise it goes at the end of the home, one level deeper than the home's heading.
- The move commit changes only positions and heading levels: the heading text (after the `#` marks) and every body line stay byte-identical, in the same order.
- Nothing may land inside `### 5.3.2`: tests/worker-exits.test.sh:238-240 reads that range.
- The PR description lists each move with its destination and a one-line reason.
- A second, separate commit makes the only content edits this task needs, in their now-final homes: §10 (design/design.md:2428-2434) names the new guard as part of the `hygiene` stage, and the moved T-185 text (today design/design.md:5216-5219, listing what preflight checks) gains check 5. No other line changes.

Anchor invariant. Across the move commit only, for every spec in design/tasks/ and both roles, `fm_prompt_context.anchors()` yields the same set of heading texts before and after; only line numbers may change. The worker shows this in the PR with the one-time evidence script, which also shows that the non-heading lines of the move commit are unchanged as a multiset and that each moved body is contiguous and in order. After merge, only the permanent superset check in the Tests item remains, so later edits to design.md are not frozen.

Rule. Under '## Spec preflight before dispatch and repin (T-185)' (skills/firstmate/SKILL.md:1139), skills/firstmate/SKILL.md says:
- A task that lists design/design.md in its scope names, in its acceptance, the numbered section it edits (§N or §N.M).
- The edit goes inside that section: amend the text, or add a subsection at the end of that section, nested under its last numbered child if it has numbered children.
- New material about other repositories goes, as `####`, under the thematically closest numbered `### 15.M`. No new `### 15.11` or later is added at the end of the file, and no unnumbered `###` follows the last `### 15.M`.
- A task that changes no contract stated in design.md does not list design/design.md.
- When firstmate briefs a rebuild for a branch that appended a tail section to design.md, the brief tells the worker to move that section into its numbered home.
Accepted limit: §15.10 is the last numbered subsection, so two parallel tasks that both edit §15.10 itself can still meet at the end of the file. Every other home is mid-file. This is documented in the rule.

Preflight. bin/lib/fm_spec_preflight.py's prompt (:27-57) gains check 5: 'If the scope lists design/design.md, does the acceptance name the numbered section (§N or §N.M) it edits? A spec that lists design/design.md without naming one, or that adds a section after the last numbered section, is a spec gap.'

Guard. bin/ci.sh's existing `hygiene` stage (one of the fast stages, bin/ci.sh:13-14) adds a design-layout check, with these rules, ignoring lines inside fenced code blocks the same way `anchors()` does (bin/lib/fm_prompt_context.py:68-76):
- In the last `## N.` section of the file, every `###` heading's text starts with that section's number followed by a dot (`N.`). A last section with no `###` headings at all passes.
- `####` and deeper headings are allowed anywhere, because they nest under a numbered home.
- Unnumbered `###` headings in earlier sections stay legal: §1 (28), §4 (106), §8 (1815-2019) and §11 (2533, 2567).
- If design/design.md does not exist, the check passes and prints nothing, like the other hygiene checks on a partial tree, so the fixture trees in tests/ci-lints.test.sh and tests/ci-sharding.test.sh are unaffected.
A planted unnumbered `###` at the end of the last section turns the stage red.

Migration.
- Stored records are unchanged. Pins hold their own design text (bin/lib/fm_spec_pins.py:179 and :295-330), and task specs that cite section numbers keep resolving, because no number changes.
- Open branches that append a tail section go red on the new guard and conflict with the move. Their next rebuild relocates the appended section into its home, following the Rule's rebuild bullet.
- Existing specs that list design/design.md without naming a section are checked at their next preflight (dispatch or repin), when the Rule and check 5 apply. A SPEC-OK recorded for exactly a spec's current bytes is not invalidated.

Tests (fail first). Two kinds.
(1) Permanent checks that never freeze design.md or the specs:
- The committed fixture `tests/fixtures/design-anchors-before-T189.json` records, for each spec id and role, the spec's section references as they were at fixture time and the heading texts `anchors()` resolved for them on the unmoved file. It leaves out the placeholder `anchors()` yields for a missing heading ('§N (heading not present in this design)', bin/lib/fm_prompt_context.py:96-97). The permanent check feeds those recorded references, not the current design/tasks specs, to `anchors()` on the current design.md, and requires every recorded heading text still to resolve. That is a superset check: headings may be added, none may disappear.
- The guard is red on a planted unnumbered `###` at the end of the last section, green on a fenced `### ` line there, green with `####` headings at the end, green on a last `## N.` section with no `###`, silent when design/design.md is missing, and green on the moved file.
- Preflight check 5 is in the prompt (tests/spec-preflight.test.sh).
- worker-exits passes.
The fixture is generated once by a script in tests/lib from the unmoved file, and committed before the move.
(2) One-time evidence for this PR only, not a standing suite: a script in tests/lib, run by the worker, whose output goes in the PR description. It shows that the move commit leaves every non-heading line unchanged as a multiset, and that each moved body is contiguous and in order. The reviewer checks that output.
Evidence is the required GitHub check and the six gates. Workers do not run the suites.
